cards.text: In the book of Isaiah, a new voice speaks up. It's the LORD's Servant. His first words are "Listen to Me," and He's not just talking to the folks next door.

cards.question: The LORD's Servant opens with "Listen to Me." Who is He telling to listen?

cards.text: He says the LORD called Him from the womb and named Him before He was even born. Before He had a name tag, a parking spot or a single TOOTH, friend, He had a JOB.
Then He says the LORD made His mouth like a sharp sword and hid Him in the shadow of His hand. And the LORD made Him like a polished arrow.

cards.question: The LORD made His Servant like a polished arrow and hid Him in His ___.

cards.text: Then the Servant tells us exactly what the LORD said to Him: "You are My Servant, Israel." And the LORD isn't done with that sentence.

cards.question: The LORD tells His Servant that He will display His glory in Him.

cards.text: You'd think after hearing all that, the Servant would be on top of the world. Then He opens His mouth.

cards.question: The Servant says, "I have labored in ___."

cards.text: He says He spent His strength in futility. I KNOW that feeling, friend. I said it for years to the dead batteries I shared a junk drawer with, and they didn't have enough charge left to argue.

cards.question: Right after saying His work felt like it was for nothing, the Servant says His reward is with His God.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks, the One who formed the Servant from the womb for a mission. And the Servant says He's honored in the LORD's sight, and His God is His strength.

cards.question: The LORD formed His Servant to bring ___ back to Him.

cards.text: Then the LORD says raising up the tribes of Jacob is "not enough" for His Servant. Baker, if somebody told me ONE oven of cookies was not enough, I'd need to sit down. On my gold base. For a WHILE.

cards.question: Raising up Jacob's tribes isn't enough. What else will the LORD make His Servant?
The LORD's salvation through His Servant will stop at the borders of Israel.

cards.text: Now the LORD, the Redeemer and Holy One of Israel, speaks to the One the nation despised and abhorred. But the LORD has a turnaround coming.

cards.question: The Servant was despised by the nation. What will kings and princes do when they see Him?
Why will the princes bow down to the Servant?

answers.text: Because of the faithful LORD who chose Him
Because of the great army behind Him
Because of the gold He brings to them

cards.text: The LORD keeps going. In the time of favor He'll answer His Servant, and in the day of salvation He'll help Him and keep Him.

cards.question: The LORD will appoint His Servant to be a ___ for the people.

cards.text: The job list keeps going: restore the land and divide up its desolate inheritances. I write ONE to-do list a day and still lose it in my apron pocket.

cards.question: Next on the list is a word for the prisoners. What is it?

cards.text: And to those in darkness: "Show yourselves." Friend, I spent years in the dark, and if somebody had said that to me, I'd have hopped out so fast my gold base would've left a dent in the drawer.
Now it sounds like a flock on the move. They'll feed along the pathways and find pasture on every barren hill.

cards.question: Along the way, the people set free will still go hungry and thirsty.
No scorching heat, no sun beating down. Who will guide these people beside springs of water?

answers.text: The One who has compassion on them
The princes who bow before Him
The elders of the tribes of Israel

cards.text: Then the LORD says He'll turn all His mountains into roads and raise up His highways. I lose my MIND when one lane is closed, and the LORD is turning MOUNTAINS into roads.

cards.question: Then the LORD says, "Behold," and looks out into the distance. What's coming?
The LORD names the land of Aswan as one of the faraway places they'll come from.

cards.text: Then the heavens, the earth and even the mountains are told to shout for joy and break forth in song. MOUNTAINS, friend, and I can't even get my oven timer to beep on key.

cards.question: Why are the heavens, the earth and the mountains told to celebrate?

answers.text: The LORD has comforted His people

cards.question: The passage ends with a promise: the LORD will have ___ on His afflicted ones.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 2 quotes "Listen to Me.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "You are My Servant, Israel.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "I have labored in ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card cites Isaiah 49:1-3, but it only tells verse 1 (the Servant saying "Listen to Me" to faraway listeners). Verses 2 and 3 are told on later cards. The citation should be Isaiah 49:1.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup line "He's not just talking to the folks next door" rules out the wrong answer "The priests in Jerusalem" on card 2. That leaves the baker only two answers to pick from.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has three separate images from verse 2: the mouth like a sharp sword, being hidden in the shadow of His hand, and being made like a polished arrow. That is more than two beats.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The setup says the Servant should be "on top of the world" and then hints that what He says next will be a letdown. That rules out both positive wrong answers on card 9 ("joy" and "peace"), so the only answer left is "vain."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke compares the Servant's futile labor to Papa Dorin's time in the junk drawer. But in the drawer he wasn't laboring at all, so the action doesn't match. The joke also adds to his backstory: he says he told the batteries this "for years," but the backstory says he went quiet and didn't talk much. It also says the batteries had no charge left to argue, while the backstory says the batteries argued over who had the most charge.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The setup "But the LORD has a turnaround coming" tells the baker the kings' reaction will be positive. That rules out both negative wrong answers on card 18 ("Turn and walk away" and "Laugh and look away").

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question asks what kings and princes will do, and the right answer is "Rise and bow down." But in Isaiah 49:7 the kings rise and the princes bow down. The right answer isn't true for each group on its own.

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both. When a question covers more than one group, like the sea creatures and the birds, the right answer must be true for every group in it.

findings.problem: The joke says his gold base would have left a dent in the drawer. In the backstory, he only gets the gold base after the angel renews him, so he didn't have it in the drawer. The line also suggests nobody ever called him out of the dark, but the angel did.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The right answer, "The One who has compassion on them," shows the baker the word "compassion." Card 14 later asks the baker to fill in "the LORD will have ___ on His afflicted ones," and the answer is "compassion."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card says the heavens, the earth and the mountains are all told to shout for joy and break forth in song. In Isaiah 49:13 the heavens shout for joy, the earth rejoices, and the mountains break forth in song. The card gives each one actions the text gives to another.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
